questions.question: Which of the following oxides is classified as an acidic oxide because it reacts with water to form an acidic solution?
questions.explanation: Sulfur trioxide (SO₃) is a non-metal oxide that reacts with water to form sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), making it an acidic oxide (acid anhydride). CaO and Na₂O are basic oxides, while CO is a neutral oxide.

questions.question: According to the Arrhenius theory, an acid is defined as any chemical substance that:

options.text: Produces hydroxide ions (OH⁻) as the only negative ions in aqueous solution.
Produces hydrogen ions (H⁺) or hydronium ions (H₃O⁺) as the only positive ions in aqueous solution.
Accepts an electron pair from a donor molecule.
Donates an electron pair to a metal cation.

questions.explanation: The Arrhenius concept defines an acid as a compound that dissociates in aqueous solution to release hydrogen ions (H⁺) or hydronium ions (H₃O⁺) as the sole cations.

questions.question: What color does phenolphthalein indicator turn when added to an aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colorless in acidic and neutral solutions (pH < 8.3) and turns bright pink/magenta in basic solutions (pH > 8.3).

questions.question: Oxides that do not react with either acids or bases to form salts are known as neutral oxides. Which of the following is a neutral oxide?
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide (NO), carbon monoxide (CO), and dinitrogen monoxide (N₂O) are neutral oxides because they display neither acidic nor basic properties and do not react with acids or bases to form salts.

questions.question: Which three chemical elements are classified as primary plant macronutrients required in large amounts for crop growth, forming the foundation of commercial NPK fertilizers?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K) are the primary macronutrients essential for plant development and are the main components of synthetic NPK fertilizers.

questions.question: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is an amphoteric oxide. What products are formed when ZnO reacts with excess concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?

options.text: Sodium zincate (Na₂ZnO₂ or Na₂[Zn(OH)₄]) and water

questions.explanation: Amphoteric oxides like ZnO react with strong bases to yield complex salts and water. With NaOH, zinc oxide forms sodium zincate (Na₂ZnO₂ or Na₂[Zn(OH)₄]) and water.

questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.001 M aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl), assuming complete ionization?
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong monoprotic acid, so [H⁺] = 0.001 M = 10⁻³ M. The pH is calculated as pH = -log[H⁺] = -log(10⁻³) = 3.0.

questions.question: Sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃) is produced by the partial neutralization of carbonic acid (H₂CO₃) with sodium hydroxide (NaOH). How is NaHCO₃ classified?
questions.explanation: Acid salts contain ionizable hydrogen atoms resulting from the incomplete neutralization of polyprotic acids (e.g., NaHCO₃ or NaH₂PO₄).

questions.question: Which pair of aqueous salt solutions will undergo a double displacement precipitation reaction to yield an insoluble white precipitate of barium sulfate (BaSO₄)?
questions.explanation: Mixing soluble BaCl₂ and soluble Na₂SO₄ causes a double displacement reaction forming insoluble barium sulfate precipitate: BaCl₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq).

questions.question: Sodium peroxide (Na₂O₂) reacts with dilute sulfuric acid to produce sodium sulfate and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂). What is the oxidation state of oxygen in peroxide compounds?
questions.explanation: In peroxides such as Na₂O₂ and H₂O₂, oxygen atoms are linked by an O-O single covalent bond, giving oxygen a characteristic oxidation state of -1.

questions.question: Diammonium phosphate (DAP) is a widely used compound fertilizer in Ethiopian agriculture. What is the correct chemical formula of DAP?
questions.explanation: Diammonium phosphate (DAP) has the chemical formula (NH₄)₂HPO₄, providing both nitrogen and phosphorus nutrients to agricultural soils.

questions.question: A student mixes 50.0 mL of 0.20 M HCl solution with 50.0 mL of 0.10 M NaOH solution. What is the pH of the resulting solution at 25 °C?
What is the percentage by mass of water of crystallization in blue vitriol, hydrated copper(II) sulfate (CuSO₄·5H₂O)? (Molar masses: CuSO₄ = 159.6 g/mol, H₂O = 18.0 g/mol)

An unknown solid powder X reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to evolve a colorless gas that turns limewater milky. When heated strongly, X decomposes into a basic oxide Y and the same gas. What are the chemical identities of X and Y?

options.text: X is Sodium chloride (NaCl); Y is Sodium metal (Na)
X is Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃); Y is Calcium oxide (CaO)
X is Ammonium nitrate (NH₄NO₃); Y is Nitrous oxide (N₂O)
X is Copper(II) sulfate (CuSO₄); Y is Copper oxide (CuO)

questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) reacts with HCl to release CO₂ gas, which forms a milky white CaCO₃ precipitate with limewater. Heating CaCO₃ thermally decomposes it into solid basic calcium oxide (CaO) and CO₂ gas.

questions.question: Why must farmers avoid applying agricultural lime (Ca(OH)₂ or CaCO₃) simultaneously with ammonium-based fertilizers like ammonium sulfate ((NH₄)₂SO₄)?

options.text: Lime oxidizes ammonium ions into toxic chlorine gas.
Basic lime reacts with ammonium ions to release volatile ammonia gas (NH₃), causing significant atmospheric nitrogen loss.
Lime turns ammonium fertilizers into an insoluble stone matrix that roots cannot absorb.
Lime causes extreme soil acidity that destroys soil flora.

questions.explanation: Ammonium salts are acidic. When mixed with basic slaked lime, an acid-base neutralization reaction occurs: (NH₄)₂SO₄ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaSO₄ + 2H₂O + 2NH₃(g). The released ammonia gas escapes into the atmosphere, causing loss of nitrogen fertilizer.
